question:
An elderly 74-year-old female with a history of Rheumatoid arthritis and osteoporosis is evaluated for a
displaced, severely comminuted fracture of the olecranon that involves 40% of its proximal portion.
What is the most appropriate surgical intervention for this case? Answer Choices: (A) Tension band
wiring (B) Partial olecranon excision with tendon repair (C) Open reduction and internal fixation with
plating (D) Conservative management with immobilization (E) Fragment excision and triceps
advancement (F) Intramedullary nailing (G) Bone grafting with structural support (H) External fixation
device application (I) Total elbow arthroplasty (J) Lag screw and neutralization plating
 A. Partial olecranon excision with tendon repair
B. Fragment excision and triceps advancement
C. External fixation device application
D. Conservative management with immobilization
E. Total elbow arthroplasty
F. Open reduction and internal fixation with plating
G. Intramedullary nailing
H. Tension band wiring
I. Lag screw and neutralization plating
J. Bone grafting with structural support
